title: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 2](/bible/2-samuel/2)

**[2 Samuel 2:1-4](/bible/2-samuel/2#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/2#v1)</sup> And it came to pass after this, that David enquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the Lord said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/2#v2)</sup> So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabal’s wife the Carmelite.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/2#v3)</sup> And his men that were with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/2#v4)</sup> And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, That the men of Jabesh–gilead were they that buried Saul.

- David inquired of the Lord whether he should go up into any of the cities of Judah, and the Lord said, Go up, unto Hebron. David did not move to take the kingdom until he asked whether it was time to be king.
- David went up with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite, and with every man and his household, and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
- The men of Judah came and there anointed David king over the house of Judah. He was raised up because the Most High had anointed him to be the next king over Israel.

**[2 Samuel 2:5-11](/bible/2-samuel/2#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/2#v5)</sup> And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh–gilead, and said unto them, Blessed be ye of the Lord, that ye have shewed this kindness unto your lord, even unto Saul, and have buried him.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/2#v6)</sup> And now the Lord shew kindness and truth unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/2#v7)</sup> Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be ye valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/2#v8)</sup> But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, took Ish–bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/2#v9)</sup> And made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/2#v10)</sup> Ish–bosheth Saul’s son was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/2#v11)</sup> And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

- David sent to the men of Jabeshgilead who had buried Saul, blessing them for the kindness shown to their lord, and telling them Judah had anointed him king over them.
- Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul and made him king over Gilead and Israel; Ishbosheth was forty years old and reigned two years, while Judah followed David. David reigned in Hebron over Judah seven years and six months.

**[2 Samuel 2:12-23](/bible/2-samuel/2#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/2#v12)</sup> And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish–bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/2#v13)</sup> And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/2#v14)</sup> And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/2#v15)</sup> Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, which pertained to Ish–bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/2#v16)</sup> And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkath–hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/2#v17)</sup> And there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/2#v18)</sup> And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/2#v19)</sup> And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/2#v20)</sup> Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Art thou Asahel? And he answered, I am.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/2#v21)</sup> And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from following of him.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/2#v22)</sup> And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/2#v23)</sup> Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth rib, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.

- Abner and the servants of Ishbosheth met Joab and the servants of David at the pool of Gibeon, sitting on opposite sides. Abner said, Let the young men arise and play, meaning let them compete and battle one another; the Lord is a man of war, and such contests were done in that day.
- Twelve of Benjamin and twelve of David's servants caught each his fellow by the head and thrust the sword in his fellow's side, so they fell down together, and that place was called Helkathhazzurim. Abner and the men of Israel were beaten before the servants of David.
- Asahel, one of the three sons of Zeruiah, was as light of foot as a wild roe, meaning he was fast, and he pursued Abner and would not turn aside. Abner warned him again and again to turn off and take another man's armor, not wanting to have to kill him and face Joab his brother.
- When Asahel refused to turn aside, Abner smote him with the hinder end of the spear under the fifth rib, and he died there. A strong thrust is needed to drive a spear through a man, and Abner was strong. Those who came to the place stood still; the lesson is to take heed to the warning and not keep testing a man.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 15:3](/bible/exodus/15#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/15#v3)</sup> The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.

    The LORD is a man of war; contests of strength were known among His people.

**[2 Samuel 2:24-32](/bible/2-samuel/2#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/2-samuel/2#v24)</sup> Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that lieth before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-samuel/2#v25)</sup> And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/2-samuel/2#v26)</sup> Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from following their brethren?
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-samuel/2#v27)</sup> And Joab said, As God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/2-samuel/2#v28)</sup> So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/2-samuel/2#v29)</sup> And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/2-samuel/2#v30)</sup> And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/2-samuel/2#v31)</sup> But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner’s men, so that three hundred and threescore men died.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/2-samuel/2#v32)</sup> And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which was in Beth–lehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.

- Joab and Abishai pursued Abner until sundown, and the children of Benjamin gathered to Abner in one troop and stood on the top of a hill. Abner had rounded up his men and stood ready.
- Abner called to Joab, asking whether the sword should devour forever, and warned that it would be bitterness in the latter end; he asked how long before Joab bade the people return from following their brethren. Joab answered that unless Abner had spoken, the people would have gone up in the morning, and he blew the trumpet and the people stood still and fought no more.
- Abner and his men walked all that night and came to Mahanaim. Of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel were missing, but they had smitten of Abner's men three hundred and threescore. They buried Asahel at Bethlehem, and Joab and his men came to Hebron at break of day.
